why: Reproduced by driving _gate-suite.html?state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across at 1024/1280/1440/1920. Below the axis the .b-date top is 751.9 for the one-line titles (Send the invitations, Venue walk-through) and 774.4 for the two-line one (Choose the evening music) at 1440 and 1920 - a 22.5px step, and the identical 22.5px step at 1024/1280 (847.9 vs 870.4). Above the axis every .b-date top is 623 at 1440/1920 including the two-line Menu tasting, so the asymmetry is exactly as described: .b-copy is bottom-anchored above and top-anchored below, and only the top-anchored side lets a wrapped title push its date down a line.
sharpenedFix: The seat is right about the fault and wrong about the fix in two ways, both measured. (1) Its display:flex on .b-title destroys the horizontal centring the across measure depends on: with flex-direction row the anonymous text item shrinks to max-content and justify-content defaults to flex-start, so text-align:center becomes a no-op. Injected at 1440 it moved Wedding day from left 1235.6 to 1158 (-77.6px off its mark), Final guest numbers -16.4px, Venue walk-through -16.8px, Send the invitations -18.2px - every single-line label knocked off the tick it names. (2) Its claim that above the axis nothing moves is true of the glyphs but its stated cost is false: placeAcross already derives --step from the TALLEST .b-copy, so no extra leading is reserved either way. Use instead the one below-scoped declaration, no flex: [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-side="below"] .b-title { min-height: calc(2 * var(--lead-body) * var(--size-body)); }. Injected and measured: below dates all land on 774.4 at 1440/1920 and 870.4 at 1280, above side byte-identical, every glyph box left/right unchanged, --step stays 96px, --rule-y stays 122px, measure height stays 244px. Note the 2-line constant is fixture-bound: a title that ever wraps to three lines re-opens the step. The general form is for placeAcross to clear and re-measure a --title-h (max rendered .b-title height) in the pass it already runs over .b-away and .b-copy, and use min-height: var(--title-h); it must reset the property before measuring or the min-height becomes self-sticky.

why: Reproduced to the pixel. Driving _gate-suite.html?state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across and clicking the .b-grab for Send the invitations, then settling 1.4s: at 1440x960 the sheet scrolls 113px and .b-edit lands at top 859, height 554, 101px visible, 0 of 4 steppers on screen; at 1440x1000 and 1920x1000, 28px visible; at 1280x900, 5px visible; via Add a moment at 1280x900, 0px. The DOWN layout at the same widths is correct (285-385px visible, 4/4 steppers at 1440 and above). Focus does land on .b-edit but every focus call in this file passes preventScroll:true (src/timeline.js:2019 and land() at :2032), so only the next Tab recovers the panel - I measured visibility jump from 101px to 553.6px on one Tab. The gate assertion at interaction-check.mjs:875 counts .b-grab handles on screen, never the editor, exactly as the seat says.
sharpenedFix: The seat diagnosed the symptom and missed the root cause, which sharpens the fix. keepInBand (src/timeline.js:1526) computes the row position as measureEl.top + away * data-px + push. data-px is 18 and away is a DAY COUNT (16/23/37/44/51/65/79), so in the across orientation - where away maps to X, not Y - it is scrolling to a fabricated vertical coordinate 414px below the measure for a row that is actually beside it. That is why it scrolls 113px to nowhere at open, and it will also fire a spurious 18px or 126px scroll after every stepper press, since each step changes away. So: (1) in keepInBand, when measureEl carries data-across=true, the row arithmetic must not run at all - there is no vertical row to follow; correct the PANEL instead. (2) Keep the seat scope (!fixed && !paneScrolls, the .app.sheet band) rather than gating on across alone, because I measured the DOWN layout at 1280x900 resolving to the same band with 0 of 4 steppers on screen (285px of 554 visible) - it needs the same correction. Leave the fixed branch alone: at 390x844 and 768x1024 the panel is position:fixed and already shows 538/538 with 4/4 steppers. Simulated the panel-based minimum correction (same pad=24, same too-tall re-centre fallback) at five sizes: panel goes to 554/554 visible and 4/4 steppers on screen at 1280x900, 1280x1000, 1440x960, 1440x1000 and 1920x1000, with grab handles still visible 3/7 at 1280x900, 6/7 at 1280x1000 and 7/7 at 1440 and above - all above the gate floor of 1.

why: Re-measured at 1920x1000 on timeline.owner-flight, across. The rail computes to y=682.4 (seat said 682). Outward distance of each element optical centre from the rail: ABOVE - number 35.1, date 51.7, title 73.7 (84.9 for the two-line Menu tasting); BELOW - number 35.1, title 55.2 (66.5 two-line), date 77.2. Every one of the seat numbers reproduces. The day count is mirrored to 0.1px on both sides and the rank stacking is explicitly radial (rank * step outward from --rule-y), so the coordinate system has already committed to mirroring; .b-copy is the one block where document order survives the mirror. I confirmed the down layout and the phone read number-then-title-then-date, so the four above-rail moments are the only place in the product that reads number-date-title.
sharpenedFix: The seat fix is correct and I verified it does not break anything, which is not obvious - flex on this block is the same move that wrecks the across labels in across-date-row-staircase. Injecting [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-side="above"] .b-copy { display:flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; } at 1920: .b-grab is position:absolute so the handle box is byte-identical ([440,575,168,63]); .b-copy box unchanged; the title box stays 168px wide at the same left, so text-align:center survives (column direction keeps align-items:stretch - this is why column-reverse is safe where row-flex is not); --step stays 96px, --away-h 18px, measure height 244px. Result: dates land at 77.2 outward on BOTH sides exactly, titles at 58.3 above against 55.2 below, down from an 18.5px title split to 3.1px. Two additions the seat missed. (1) Close the residual 3.1px by also reversing the block internal gap/margin above the rail, otherwise the leading edge margin that was under the title is now under the date. (2) State the a11y position explicitly: DOM order stays title-then-date while the visual order above the rail becomes date-then-title, and that is the correct trade here because the grab handle carries the whole sentence as aria-label so the copy is never the AT reading path, and the unchanged DOM order is what already matches the down layout.

why: Re-sampled the crossing myself at 1440x960 (notes.seam, send, then open-task) on 79 rAF frames. On the arriving card only transform changes - 14 distinct values easing from matrix(0.994,0,0,0.994,0,-2) to identity. opacity, background-color, border-color, box-shadow, outline, filter, ::before and ::after each hold exactly ONE distinct value for the whole crossing; the tray styles hold one; the head string holds one. After settle at 1440 and 1280 the only computed property that differs from its lane neighbour is transform (matrix identity vs none), and the card is 4th of 4 in To do. data-settling survives as an empty attribute that draws nothing. So the entire visual event is a 2px rise and a 1.5px width change on a 256px card, which is not perceptible.
sharpenedFix: Two corrections, both measured. (1) The seat missed that the arrival ALREADY has a designed marker and it is being suppressed, not missing: document.activeElement IS the arrived card at 1440, 1280 and 390. Cross by keyboard instead of pointer and the same card wears outline 2px solid rgb(79,70,229) plus box-shadow rgba(79,70,229,0.16) 0 0 0 4px - a loud, unambiguous here-is-what-you-sent. It vanishes on the pointer crossing only because the focus is programmatic and :focus-visible is false. So do not invent a treatment: on open-task set data-arrived and draw it with the EXISTING focus-visible ring (2px indigo outline + 4px indigo-16 halo), clearing on blur or first interaction. One treatment, one meaning - you are on this card - no new colour, and it matches what the keyboard path already shows. (2) The seat fix as written collides: there is a live [data-next] card on the same board at the same moment (demo-t-02, Menu tasting at The Orchard) already wearing rgba(79,70,229,0.32) 0 0 0 1px. Painting data-arrived with that identical ring puts two indigo hairlines on one board meaning two different things. Also drop the 30-second framing - the thirty-second window is a Notes construct (src/notes.js) and there is no undo bar on the Tasks side after the crossing; clear the attribute on blur/first interaction/next mount instead. scrollIntoView is harmless insurance but not the fix: I measured the card on screen at 1440, 1280 and 390. The bigger settle (translateY -12px) is optional taste; the audit checks motion duration and easing steps only, not distance, so it would not trip the gate either way.

why: Every number reproduces. At 1920 on tasks.board the grid computes to 372px 372px 372px 172px 372px; the last card right edge is 1764 while .headActions and .viewTools both end at 1874 - a 110px break. The contract is exact at 1280 (1234/1234), 1440 (1394/1394), 1600, 1750 and 1810 (1764/1764), then breaks 40px at 1850, 110px at 1920 and 200px at 2048 and 2560. tasks.compact behaves identically; tasks.dense, with no empty lane, aligns to the pixel at every width up to 2560, so the grid is capable of it. The CSS states the intent it fails, verbatim at src/tasks.css:638-639: the four lanes with work in them take the room. The sheet head spans 100..1902, optical centre 1001, against a board track centre of 946 - the 55px offset the seat describes.
sharpenedFix: The seat rule is correct and I verified it by injection: break goes to 0 at 1850, 1920, 2048 and 2560 and is a byte-for-byte no-op at 1200, 1280, 1440 and 1810; tracks at 1920 become 399.5/399.5/399.5/172/399.5 exactly as claimed; no new horizontal scroll on the board or the document at any width. Two things to write into it that the seat left out. (1) The 422 constant is the exactly-one-collapsed-lane case only. Write it as its arithmetic - minmax(196px, calc(372px + (372px - 172px) / 4)) - so the next reader sees why. A board with TWO collapsed lanes is reachable by a person (tick out every card in a lane) and I measured the rule there: tracks 422/422/422/172/172, break 504px instead of the ideal 0. It is still an improvement, never a runaway, but if the panel wants it general add the sibling rule for two collapsed lanes at calc(372px + 400px / 3). (2) Name the consequence the seat does not: with the fix the same card is 376px wide at 1920 and 398px at 2048 on a board with an empty lane, against 348px on a full board at the same width. That is the stated intent (the lanes with work take the room) but it does mean the card measure now varies with whether an unrelated lane happens to be empty; if that is unacceptable, the alternative is to cap the ceiling at 372 and instead shrink the board box to its tracks, which trades the dead column for a board that no longer starts on the sheet leading edge - a worse trade against justify-content: safe start, which the CSS calls load-bearing.

why: Ran page.accessibility.snapshot({interestingOnly:false}) on a board card at 1440 myself. The article comes back name=Confirm marquee sides with the hire company, description=Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not, they need the call by Thursday. Mara & Finn. High priority. - and then as CHILDREN: a paragraph carrying the title a second time, a generic node carrying that entire description string a second time (the .sr span itself), a paragraph carrying the note a third time, a button carrying the tag a third time, and text carrying High / priority a third time. src/tasks.js:461 builds the span with class sr and id cd-<id> and no aria-hidden, so the CSS hides it from sight only. 13 cards on tasks.board (971 characters of pure duplication) and 32 on tasks.dense (1377).
sharpenedFix: The seat fix is right and I verified the load-bearing half of it in the same engine rather than trusting the spec: with aria-hidden="true" set on the cd- span, the article description comes back byte-identical (accname traversal from an aria-describedby reference includes hidden subtrees) while the duplicate generic node loses its text from the tree. Ship it exactly as written at src/tasks.js:461. Three scoping notes to write into the change. (1) Scope it to the cd- span alone, not to .sr generally - the other describedby target in this file, tn- at src/tasks.js:1139, points at a VISIBLE .trayNote paragraph, and hiding that would delete real text from the reading order. (2) The title is still spoken twice after the fix (article name plus the visible .cardTitle paragraph) and that is correct - do not extend the fix to .cardTitle. (3) State the blast radius: this is the board and dense surfaces only. At 1024 the board is a list and carries no .card elements at all, so the list rows are not affected and must not be swept into the same edit.
